items.q: Hypoalbuminemia in nephrotic syndrome arises from urinary loss of albumin together with:
items.exp: Urinary loss of albumin; ↓ compensation by liver. (Book p757)

items.q: The nail sign illustrated for hypoalbuminemia, a white transverse line, is:
items.exp: Sign: white transverse line – Muehrcke's line. (Book p757)

items.q: For nephrotic edema the book ranks the theories as:
The underfill sequence runs hypoalbuminemia → loss of capillary oncotic pressure → fluid transfer to interstitium, giving periorbital puffiness and pedal edema plus:
opts: ↓ effective circulatory volume with 2° RAS activation
↑ effective circulatory volume with ANP release
items.exp: ↓ effective circulatory volume → 2° RAS activation → aldosterone → Na+, water retention. (Book p757)

items.q: Fill up: In the underfill theory, 2° RAS activation causes release of ______, retaining Na+ and water as intravascular edema.
items.exp: 2° RAS activation → release of aldosterone → retention of Na+, water. (Book p757)
